categories.title: Pieces on a board
categories.blurb: The oldest shelf: boards scratched in stone, dice made of bone, and the slow invention of the race, the capture and the checkmate.

categories.title: Cards in hand
categories.blurb: Paper, ink and a hand you keep hidden: trick-taking, betting, shedding and the solitaires that need only one player.

categories.title: Dice, tiles and counters
categories.blurb: Bones, cubes, dominoes and mahjong tiles: games where the piece is drawn, rolled or matched rather than moved.

categories.title: Words, numbers and puzzles
categories.blurb: Letters, grids and physical riddles: the games a single player can carry in a pocket or a newspaper.

categories.title: Children's and playground games
categories.blurb: The games children teach each other: chasing, hiding, skipping, rhyming and the small rituals of a schoolyard.

categories.title: Balls, bats and races
categories.blurb: Balls, bats, rackets and cues: the codified sports and the older games they grew from.

categories.title: Modern board games
categories.blurb: The commercial board game from the Victorian parlour to the Eurogame: family races, trading, co-operation and tile-laying.

categories.title: Tabletop worlds
categories.blurb: Dice, paper and miniature armies: role-playing campaigns, wargames and the long games that live in a box for years.

categories.title: Collectible cards and children's tabletop
categories.blurb: The bridge between a toy and a game: collectible cards, dexterity toys and the first tabletop games a child owns.

categories.title: Arcade and early electronic
categories.blurb: The coin-op century: oscilloscopes, vector screens, maze chases and the arcade cabinet as a public room.

categories.title: Console and computer games
categories.blurb: The home screen: text adventures, consoles, shooters, simulations and the games that became a mass culture.

categories.title: Online, mobile and networked
categories.blurb: The networked game: persistent worlds, team shooters, battle royales and the phone in every pocket.

categories.title: Open-source and free games
categories.blurb: Games whose code or rules are free to read, run, change and share: the open-source shelf, from roguelikes to chess servers.

categories.title: Party, live and social games
categories.blurb: The game played in a room: acting, guessing, bluffing, deduction, dares and the escape room.
